creativity.reason: Level 0: the filing describes the business fully and shows no creating or enabling of creative work.

community.reason: Level 2: all current activities are employee development, so the score is capped at 2; the only external community investment (the Foundation gift) is past.

cross_cultural.reason: Level 1: only workforce demographic statistics and general 'inclusive work environment' language, with no specific internal, customer-access or community program described.

entrepreneurship.reason: Level 1: the company serves many small-business customers and lends to them, but describes no specific enabling program such as startup financing, grants or accelerators.

notes: The JPMorgan Chase Foundation $1.0B Visa-share contribution (E5) was made in Q2 2024; the FY2025 MD&A cites it only as a prior-year item, so it is recorded as past and not scored. The Public Responsibility Committee's oversight of 'community investment' is governance language with no activity described, so it was not scored. Client fraud 'education and awareness trainings' is a risk control or customer-education item and was not counted. Required Code of Conduct and compliance training count as compliance training only. Lending to small businesses (~$33B; 7.4M customers) was treated as serving rather than enabling, choosing the lower level when torn. The Item 7 text is targeted excerpts only. Community and Cross-cultural coverage is marked insufficient because the 10-K barely discusses external community programs or inclusion practices beyond demographics, which triggers the automated second look with the company's sustainability report.
